hero.headline: St. Lucie County schools to close Friday as heavy rain threatens morning commute
hero.teaser: St. Lucie County schools will be closed Friday, Nov. 20, as additional heavy rain threatens the morning trip to school in already saturated areas, district officials announced Thur
hero.body:
St. Lucie County schools will be closed Friday, Nov. 20, as additional heavy rain threatens the morning trip to school in already saturated areas, district officials announced Thursday. The district said it made the decision out of caution because the heaviest rainfall could coincide with the arrival of students and staff.

 After a break in the rain Thursday afternoon, the National Weather Service is forecasting another 3 to 4 inches or more overnight and into Friday morning, according to the district. The heaviest rain is expected around the time students and staff would normally travel to school. District officials cited student and staff safety, along with saturated conditions throughout the community, as the reasons for closing schools.

 All after-school programs scheduled for Friday are canceled, including aftercare, activities and athletic events. The closure means students will begin their Thanksgiving holiday early. Students are scheduled to return to school Monday, Nov. 30.

 District officials will decide later Friday whether the SAT scheduled for Saturday, Nov. 21, will take place. The district said it will communicate that decision to families as soon as possible.

cards.teaser: The Martin County Sheriff’s Office is asking for the public’s help finding Stephen Levi Cotela, 15, who was last seen running north toward Jonathan Dickinson State Park. His last k
cards.body:
The Martin County Sheriff’s Office is asking for the public’s help finding Stephen Levi Cotela, 15, who was last seen running north toward Jonathan Dickinson State Park. His last known location was near SE County Line Road and SE Harken Terrace in Tequesta.

 Cotela has been missing since 3:30 p.m., according to the Sheriff’s Office. Deputies said he got out of his father’s vehicle after an argument and ran toward the park.

 Cotela is 5 feet 5 inches tall, weighs approximately 120 to 130 pounds and has black hair and brown eyes. He was last seen wearing a gray t-shirt, black sweatpants and sandals.

cards.headline: Indian River County remains under Flood Watch as more heavy rain threatens
cards.teaser: Road closures and standing water have affected Vero Lake Estates and other parts of Indian River County. Emergency officials urge residents to avoid unnecessary travel as additional rain could worsen flooding.
cards.body:
Indian River County remains under a Flood Watch as additional heavy rain through Saturday threatens areas already saturated by recent rainfall, the National Weather Service said Thursday. With roads affected by closures or standing water, county emergency officials urged residents to stay home unless they need to travel.

 The National Weather Service office in Melbourne forecasts a 40% to 60% chance of 3 to 6 inches of additional rain along the east-central Florida coast through Saturday. Saturated soil has made many areas more prone to flooding. If the most likely rainfall totals materialize, scattered pockets of flooding could develop along the coast.

 The forecast also puts the chance of higher-end totals of 8 to 10 inches or more at 10% in some locations. Those amounts would bring a risk of impactful flash flooding.

 Multiple roads in the Vero Lake Estates area and elsewhere in Indian River County have had closures or standing water this week because of the saturated ground. The Indian River County Emergency Operations Center continues to monitor weather and road conditions. It warned that floodwater and road damage can be difficult to see after dark.

 Residents should check the county’s road closure map before traveling and never drive through flooded roads or around barricades, emergency officials said. A road may be unsafe even if the map does not show it as closed.

cards.headline: TRICARE authorizes emergency prescription refills in Florida through Nov. 29
cards.teaser: The Defense Health Agency has authorized temporary emergency prescription refills through Nov. 29 for TRICARE beneficiaries in flood-affected Florida counties, including Martin, St
cards.body:
The Defense Health Agency has authorized temporary emergency prescription refills through Nov. 29 for TRICARE beneficiaries in flood-affected Florida counties, including Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River. Beneficiaries needing a refill should take their prescription bottle to any TRICARE retail network pharmacy.

 If the bottle is unavailable or its label is damaged or missing, beneficiaries should contact Express Scripts or a retail network pharmacy for assistance. To find a network pharmacy, beneficiaries can call Express Scripts at 1-877-363-1303.

 When possible, beneficiaries should use the pharmacy where their prescription was originally filled, according to the agency. A prescription filled by a retail chain may also be filled at another location operated by that chain. Beneficiaries whose prescribing clinician is available can ask the clinician to call a new prescription into a network pharmacy.

 The waiver applies to counties affected by fall flooding. It also covers Brevard, Broward, DeSoto, Duval, Flagler, Glades, Hardee, Hendry, Highlands, Miami-Dade, Monroe, Okeechobee, Palm Beach, Putnam, Seminole and Volusia counties.

 TRICARE beneficiaries other than active-duty service members may also receive urgent care from any TRICARE-authorized urgent care center or provider without a referral, according to the Defense Health Agency. That option allows beneficiaries to seek nonemergency treatment when their primary care provider is unavailable because of an emergency.

 Anyone who reasonably believes they are experiencing a medical emergency should call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board reinstates Matthew Theobald, awards back pay
cards.teaser: The board rescinded the Spectrum Academy teacher’s suspension and termination after a judge ruled his comments about Charlie Kirk’s death did not justify dismissal.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board voted this week to reinstate Spectrum Academy teacher Matthew Theobald and rescind his suspension and termination after adopting a judge’s recommendation. The judge had ruled that Theobald’s social media comments about conservative activist Charlie Kirk’s death did not justify suspension or dismissal. Theobald will also be awarded back pay and benefits through June 30.

 The Martin County School District sought to dismiss Theobald over several online comments following Kirk’s murder in Utah in September 2025. The school board voted to suspend Theobald without pay and recommended his termination. Both parties agreed to an administrative hearing to address the matter.

 In June, the judge ruled that the school board failed to prove Theobald engaged in immorality or willful neglect of duty, which would have been grounds for dismissal. The judge also found that Theobald’s Facebook comments did not disrupt his students or the learning environment, or reduce any teacher’s ability to teach. District leadership said after the ruling that it would review the recommendation.

 School board member Marsha Powers said she voted in favor of the decision but questioned the process. “I have serious concerns about the process that brought this matter before a judge who does not live or work in the community,” Powers said.

 Board member Tony Anderson said he understood Powers’ concerns but noted that the board had already placed the issue in the judge’s hands. “It’s a decision we have to live with,” Anderson said.

St. Lucie County schools will be closed Friday, Nov. 20, as additional heavy rain threatens the morning trip to school in already saturated areas, district officials announced Thursday. The district said it made the decision out of caution because the heaviest rainfall could coincide with the arrival of students and staff.

 After a break in the rain Thursday afternoon, the National Weather Service is forecasting another 3 to 4 inches or more overnight and into Friday morning, according to the district. The heaviest rain is expected around the time students and staff would normally travel to school. District officials cited student and staff safety, along with saturated conditions throughout the community, as the reasons for closing schools.

 All after-school programs scheduled for Friday are canceled, including aftercare, activities and athletic events. The closure means students will begin their Thanksgiving holiday early. Students are scheduled to return to school Monday, Nov. 30.

 District officials will decide later Friday whether the SAT scheduled for Saturday, Nov. 21, will take place. The district said it will communicate that decision to families as soon as possible.

cards.headline: Indian River County remains under Flood Watch as more heavy rain threatens
cards.teaser: Road closures and standing water have affected Vero Lake Estates and other parts of Indian River County. Emergency officials urge residents to avoid unnecessary travel as additional rain could worsen flooding.
cards.body:
Indian River County remains under a Flood Watch as additional heavy rain through Saturday threatens areas already saturated by recent rainfall, the National Weather Service said Thursday. With roads affected by closures or standing water, county emergency officials urged residents to stay home unless they need to travel.

 The National Weather Service office in Melbourne forecasts a 40% to 60% chance of 3 to 6 inches of additional rain along the east-central Florida coast through Saturday. Saturated soil has made many areas more prone to flooding. If the most likely rainfall totals materialize, scattered pockets of flooding could develop along the coast.

 The forecast also puts the chance of higher-end totals of 8 to 10 inches or more at 10% in some locations. Those amounts would bring a risk of impactful flash flooding.

 Multiple roads in the Vero Lake Estates area and elsewhere in Indian River County have had closures or standing water this week because of the saturated ground. The Indian River County Emergency Operations Center continues to monitor weather and road conditions. It warned that floodwater and road damage can be difficult to see after dark.

 Residents should check the county’s road closure map before traveling and never drive through flooded roads or around barricades, emergency officials said. A road may be unsafe even if the map does not show it as closed.
